I graded submission s1 of quiz 0001 and wrote `grades/0001-s1.json`. You got 2 of 6 right, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | wrong (M4) | The model outputs a tool request; the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | correct | A step limit is the safeguard against a stuck loop. |
| q4 | wrong (M4) | The answer is 4 model calls, not 1: three tool requests plus the final answer. |
| q5 | partial | You said the result goes back to the model, but not why. The model needs it in its next input to choose its next step or write the answer. |
| q6 | partial (M3) | Tool descriptions are right. The claim that it remembers earlier sessions on its own is wrong. |

**Where you are:** You have the loop, the step-limit safeguard and description-based tool choice down. The thing to fix is who does what. The model only writes a request for a tool, and the program runs it and calls the model again. The same idea sits behind the memory slip in q6: the model keeps nothing between sessions unless the program saves it and passes it back in.

**Next step:** Reread these before retrying:
- "Where tools run" and "The agentic loop (client tools)" in "How tool use works" (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/how-tool-use-works)
- "Turns and messages" and "Sessions and continuity" in "How the agent loop works" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop)

There were no lessons or cheat sheets yet, so every pointer goes to an official doc. I added all three docs to `RESOURCES.md`. The grade reviewer ran two passes, and the second came back with no findings.

I also added `learning-records/0003-who-runs-the-tools.md`, updated `NOTES.md`, and saved the review record in `review-records/0001-s1-grade.md`.
